acceptanceCriteria: A 47k-receipt run with per-round timing confirms or refutes the no-resume-flag hypothesis; the result is retained.
A non-detached pool acquire reaches ACQUIRED within 150 s at 47k receipts with a journal head moving every minute, with CAL-V0-116 rewritten-prefix detection intact (negative test).
PENDING answers or doctor split complete versus prefix walks with elapsed time and restart counts.
The ATR spec documents the PENDING progress member or cites PSR-V0-112.
body: GitHub #1063. V1-1617 (PR #1069) delivered: detached acquire progress (PSR-V0-112), compact help cost note (PSR-V0-114), resume after compaction (PSR-V0-115). Remaining: (1) starting the audit from a writer checkpoint was declined there because the CAL-V0-264 writer route drops CAL-V0-116 rewritten-prefix detection; orchestrator decision 2026-10-17: keep CAL-V0-116 detection, so fix speed via root cause and a faster prefix walk instead. (2) Unconfirmed hypothesis from the 1617 lane: one failed resume-base build sets a command-wide no-resume flag, so the remaining rounds of 16 each run a complete audit. (3) Linear extrapolation (not measured): 155-282 s first audit at 47k receipts, so a non-detached 150 s call cannot succeed. (4) The PENDING progress member is documented only in PSR, not ATR.
title: pool acquire stays CPU-bound for 38+ min re-walking a moving journal (GitHub #1063)
